'''Karsten Reuter''' (born 13 June 1970 in [[Offenbach am Main]]) is a German [[physicist]] and [[chemist]].

== Life and work ==

Reuter studied physics at the [[Friedrich-Alexander-Universität Erlangen-Nürnberg]] and the [[University of York]].<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=Karsten Reuter – CV|url=https://www.fhi.mpg.de/492961/CV_Reuter2020.pdf|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=8 October 2020|website=}}</ref> He conducted his doctoral studies at the CSIC [https://www.icmm.csic.es/ Instituto de Ciencia de Materiales de Madrid (ICMM)] and in Erlangen, where he received his doctorate in 1995 under Prof. Dr. Klaus Heinz for his work on electronic transport across metal-semiconductor interfaces. After [[postdoctoral studies]] at the [[Fritz Haber Institute of the Max Planck Society|Fritz-Haber-Institut (FHI) der Max-Planck-Gesellschaft (MPG)]] in Berlin and at the [https://amolf.nl/ FOM Institute for Atomic and Molecular Physics (AMOLF)] in Amsterdam, he led an Independent MPG Research Group at the FHI from 2005 to 2009 and completed his [[Habilitation]] in Theoretical Solid State Physics at the [[FU Berlin]] in 2005. From 2009 to 2020 he held the chair for [[theoretical chemistry]] at the [[Technical University of Munich]] (TUM) und was a member of the [https://www.e-conversion.de/ TUM Catalysis Research Center].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Prof. Reuter |first1=Karsten |title=TUM Catalysis Research Center |url=https://www.professoren.tum.de/en/reuter-karsten |accessdate=8 October 2020 }}{{Dead link|date=August 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> Since 2020 he is director and scientific member at the Berlin [[Fritz Haber Institute of the Max Planck Society|Fritz-Haber-Institut der MPG]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Prof. Reuter |first1=Karsten, Director |title=Theory Department, Fritz Haber Institute of the MPG |url=https://www.fhi.mpg.de/th-department |accessdate=9 October 2020}}</ref>

Reuter's research activities focus on a quantitative modeling of materials properties and functions. Specifically, he addresses processes in working catalysts and energy conversion devices such as electrolyzers, fuel cells or batteries. For this, he advances predictive-quality multiscale models and data science approaches, uniting methods and concepts from physics, chemistry, machine learning, as well as [[materials science]] and [[engineering]].

== Honors and awards ==
For his work, Reuter received multiple awards and distinctions. In 2018, he was awarded the Frontiers Award for Chemical Energy Conversion.<ref>{{cite web |last1=MPI for Chemical Energy Conversion |first1=Mülheim an der Ruhr, Germany |title=Frontiers Award for Chemical Energy Conversion |url=https://cec.mpg.de/en/news/detail-view/news/frontiers-award-fuer-prof-karsten-reuter/ |website=Prof. Karsten Reuter |accessdate=9 October 2020}}</ref> Recent visiting professorships include [[Stanford]] (2014–2015),<ref>{{cite web |last1=Professor Karsten Reuter |title=SUNCAT, Center for Interface Science and Catalysis |url=https://suncat.stanford.edu/people/karsten-reuter |website=Stanford University |accessdate=9 October 2020}}</ref> the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] (2018) and the [[Imperial College London]] (2019–2020).
